solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: German behind refined melody given to new film

parts.note: the behind is the rump, the backside

indicators.note: refined suggests something processed into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A German composer's polished tune is paired with a new film score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German behind' reads as a German at the back, but it is two separate pieces; 'refined' shuffles the melody's letters with N.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumpy Old Men is a 1993 Hollywood comedy starring Jack Lemmon and Walter Matthau.

clue.text: One soft cheese and one firm in flaky tart

indicators.note: in places the one-and-firm letters inside the rearranged pastry word
flaky pastry crumbles apart, so the letters of tart are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a firm is a company, abbreviated CO

explanation.surface: A recipe pairs a soft cheese with a firm one inside a flaky pastry tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flaky' looks like a description of the tart's pastry, but it is the signal to rearrange the word tart.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft, mild Italian whey cheese.

clue.text: Fish certainly found in another lake

indicators.note: found in tells us one word is discovered sitting inside the others

parts.note: more, as in 'one more', means another
aye is an affirmative, yes certainly

explanation.surface: An angler insists a fish is certainly to be found in some other lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A moray is a reef-dwelling eel, so the whole answer is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A moray eel is a large predatory eel of tropical reefs, a kind of fish.

clue.text: One girl said he may be French

indicators.note: said signals that the girl's name is to be heard, not read

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name, the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A girl speaks up, perhaps to say that he is French.
explanation.walkthrough: The French name Yves is pronounced just like Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Yves is a common French man's name, as in Yves Saint Laurent.

clue.text: Words, perhaps 50 more than 26

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
over means more than, as in over a hundred
26 points to entry 26-across, a corpse, and stiff is slang for a corpse

explanation.surface: A cryptic sum: fifty added to more than twenty-six makes some words.
explanation.walkthrough: The 26 is a cross-reference to the corpse clue at 26-across, giving STIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Having words with someone means a quarrel, and a lovers' tiff is a minor quarrel between partners.

clue.text: Note, note, note, note — put that up

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
N is the abbreviation for note used in footnote references

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting a piece up means writing it from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: mi again, a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A frustrated teacher keeps writing notes and orders them pinned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put that up' turns the final MI into IM, giving MI, N, IM.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note worth half a semibreve, a half note.

clue.text: "Repelled an attack" pronounced in a certain way

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the little word an is turned back to front

parts.note: a sally is a sudden attack, a sortie from a besieged position

explanation.surface: A quoted line about fending off an attack is delivered with a particular accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the first part look like speech, but 'Repelled' turns AN round to NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken through the nose describes a particular manner of pronunciation, a certain way of speaking.

clue.text: Private celebrations? House has gone for top fashion designer

indicators.note: has gone for indicates one piece is dropped and another put in its place

parts.note: a private soldier is a GI, so a GI's celebrations are GI anniversaries
Aries is the first house of the zodiac in astrology
ace means top, first-rate

explanation.surface: A grand fashion house swaps its private parties for a top designer.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping ARIES at the end of GI ANNIVERSARIES for ACE gives the Italian designer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Gianni Versace was a celebrated Italian couturier who founded the Versace label.

clue.text: Once ninety, some big changes

indicators.note: changes, read as a verb, tells us the words' letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Once someone reaches ninety, some big changes come along.
explanation.definitionFit: Once, meaning formerly or at an earlier date, is the same as in days long past.

clue.text: Empty vehicle on run up to bend

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after the previous piece

parts.note: to run up debts is to incur them

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: An empty car is driven onward, running up to a bend in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run up' looks like running, but it is the verb for running up debts.
explanation.definitionFit: To incurve is to curve inwards, to bend.

clue.text: Meat we're ready to cook? Leave the starter

indicators.note: leaving the starter means dropping the first letter of the phrase

parts.note: when we are ready to cook, the oven is on

explanation.surface: A cook announces the meat is ready to go but the starter will be skipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oven is on' run together, without its first letter, gives the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is the meat of deer.

clue.text: Bolt's partner initially two yards round the bend

parts.note: nuts and bolts go together, so a bolt's partner is a nut

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt's partner runs two yards around the bend of a track.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the sprinter Usain Bolt; the bolt here is the hardware one.
explanation.definitionFit: Round the bend is British slang for crazy, mad.

clue.text: House in Monaco next to ghastly supermarket

parts.note: grim means ghastly, horrible
Aldi is a German discount supermarket chain

explanation.surface: A royal house in Monaco stands beside a grim discount supermarket.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimaldi is the princely family that has ruled Monaco for centuries.

clue.text: Old Elgar tune's enigmatic beat?

indicators.note: enigmatic means puzzling, so the letters are jumbled into a riddle

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A music lover wonders about the mysterious rhythm of an old Elgar tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enigmatic' nods at Elgar's Enigma Variations, while rearranging O, ELGAR and TUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: To outgeneral is to outmanoeuvre an opponent by superior tactics, to beat them.

clue.text: Wanting one bent and parallel

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: to parallel something is to equate it, match it as equivalent

explanation.surface: A solver is found lacking, being one who is bent and running parallel at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parallel' is a verb here, meaning to match or equate.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanting, meaning lacking or not up to standard, is a synonym of insufficient.

clue.text: A promoter of mushy peas?

indicators.note: of here means drawn out of, so the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone is publicly championing that British chip-shop side dish, mushy peas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' marks the run inside 'mushy peas' (mashed marrowfat peas, a British side dish). The definition is loose: hype is promotion rather than a promoter, which the question mark admits.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is overblown publicity, the force that pushes a product, so it loosely stands for a promoter.

clue.text: Religious group's work extremely dubious, supported by muscle

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by means the next piece sits underneath

parts.note: if something works, it goes

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters of the word, its first and last

parts.note: quad is short for quadriceps, the thigh muscle

explanation.surface: A religious group's work is judged highly dubious, though backed by muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives DS from dubious; QUAD goes below.
explanation.definitionFit: God squad is informal, often mocking, slang for a group of evangelical Christians.

clue.text: Oriental, say, out for a walk in the park

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient

indicators.note: out means not in proper order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oriental visitor, say, goes out for a walk in the park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges E and SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A walk in the park is an idiom for something effortless, simple.

clue.text: Roll over after small child fell

indicators.note: after places the following piece behind the ones before

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a kid is a child

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a wad is a roll of banknotes

explanation.surface: A small child takes a roll and a tumble, then falls over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns WAD into DAW. A fell is a hill in northern England; Skiddaw is one in the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiddaw is one of the highest mountains in England's Lake District, where hills are called fells.

clue.text: Chinese food for one? No — kids about to tuck into horse

parts.note: for one means for example, abbreviated EG

indicators.note: to tuck into means placing the reversed piece inside the horse letters

parts.note: gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the two words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
yoof is British slang for young people, kids

explanation.surface: Someone declines Chinese food as the kids tuck into horse meat instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns both NO and the slang word for kids, giving FOOYON, which 'to tuck into' then places inside the child's word for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg foo yong is a Chinese-style omelette dish.

clue.text: National anthem is nothing about nothing

parts.note: O, a zero, means nothing
CA, short for circa, means about
nada is Spanish for nothing, used in English slang

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a national anthem is much ado about nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the anthem of the Canadian nation, sung at state events and before hockey games.

clue.text: A load of fashionable pieces in stone

indicators.note: in places the fashionable pieces inside the stone abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
hip means fashionable
chess pieces are known as men

explanation.surface: A heavy consignment of trendy stone artworks arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipment is a consignment of goods, a load sent at once.

clue.text: Doctor's struggle to produce film

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
to vie is to compete, struggle

explanation.surface: A doctor's battle to make a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A movie is a film, especially in American usage.

clue.text: F1 circuit in location of Estoril

parts.note: Spa-Francorchamps in Belgium is a Formula One racing circuit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Formula One circuit in the Estoril area.
explanation.walkthrough: Estoril is a resort near Lisbon in Portugal, so as a definition this is shaky: the Iberian peninsula is at best what the setter meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is taken as the setting of the Estoril resort and its former Grand Prix track.

clue.text: Mostly smooth beam

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to grind something is to smooth it by abrasion

explanation.surface: A smooth beam of timber, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam is to smile broadly, to grin.

clue.text: Corpse in one rotten state

parts.note: a cad is a rotter, a rotten one
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A corpse is found in a state of decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten state' paints decay, but 'one rotten' is a cad and 'state' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadaver is a dead body, especially one used for dissection.

clue.text: River with pub in the middle? Nonsense!

indicators.note: in puts the pub inside the word for the middle

parts.note: the hub is the middle of something
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A riverside village with its pub at the centre is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the middle' looks like a placement instruction, but 'the middle' is itself a piece, the hub.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is British slang for nonsense, from actors muttering the word to mimic crowd noise.

clue.text: Engineer making cycle with wood

parts.note: a wheel is a cycle, a circle
and means with, together
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: An engineer builds a bicycle out of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer something is to contrive it by scheming, which is what wheeling and dealing means.
